The newly established unit requires one row per orchestrator effect, so these three controls must be independently dispositioned rather than grouped; otherwise the task violates the exact completeness rule this commit adds.

This commit's own `kind: docs` task has no `invariants` field and `dotfiles-T128-playbook-rules-a01` is absent from the referenced design's map, so applying the rule literally makes this task—and other non-implementation docs/review tasks—impossible to approve. The failure mode this sentence is intended to prevent can therefore still result in an arbitrarily long silent wait; define a concrete elapsed-time limit or add an explicit duration field to TASKs before requiring the bus read and PING.

When this path is triggered by `scripts/regime-counters.sh`, the class is derived from the first three words of a review-comment title with no shell-safe normalization (`scripts/regime-counters.sh:143-147`). items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define threat rows per concrete changed path**

When an `allowed_files` entry is a permitted wildcard such as `scripts/orchestrator/*`, one generic row now satisfies the stated unit even if the PR changes several independently executable trust-boundary scripts. The existing T718 task demonstrates why the distinction matters: its single wildcard covers `dispatch.sh`, `three-repeat.sh`, and `bus-read.sh`, which require three different controls. Defining completeness per concrete changed file, or forbidding multi-file globs at trust boundaries, prevents a broad entry from hiding missing threat analysis.
